limitations: The optimal factor is an infinitesimal supremum over fixed C^3 radial perturbations of the unit disk with zero zeroth and first Fourier modes; it is not a global finite-deformation inequality.
No nonzero fixed perturbation attains the sharp factor; the proof of the supremum uses a sequence of high-frequency trigonometric polynomials.
The published-source comparison cannot rule out every unindexed historical equivalent.
scientific_integrity: The proof is analytic. Finite computations check the expansions but are not claimed to establish an infinite-dimensional result; independent validation is unperformed.
title: Sharp local isoperimetric control of boundary–bulk centroid displacement
